rationale:
The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.search.StructuralMatch` has three testable obligations. I found each one tested with assertions.

1. **Constructor and fields.** `StructuralMatch::new(node, excerpt)` must expose `node` and `excerpt` as public fields. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/search.rs#fn[callers_can_construct_complete_and_partial_search_results]` builds a match with `OutlineData::new(path, "fn[example]")` and the excerpt "example". It then asserts that `matches[0].node == address` and `matches[0].excerpt == "example"`. That test is an integration test in a separate crate. It can only build the struct through `new`, so it also exercises the `#[non_exhaustive]` shape.

2. **`node` identifies the enclosing outline item.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope]` runs a real structural search over `fn visible() { call(); }`. It asserts `node.path == visible.rs` and `node.selector == "fn[visible]"`. That is the enclosing function, not the file root. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/tests.rs#fn[structural_search_uses_overridden_parses_their_snapshot_and_requested_scope]` asserts the same for a custom provider: path `src/one.rs` and selector `fn[cached]`.

3. **`excerpt` is the matched byte range and may be smaller than the enclosing item.** Both search tests assert `excerpt == "call()"`. The enclosing function is `fn visible() { call(); }` and the match excludes the trailing `;`, so the excerpt really is the matched range and not the whole item. The constructor test also asserts the excerpt is stored unchanged.

The public-export test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` covers the type's presence in the public API.

I found no gap. Deeply nested enclosing items and multibyte excerpts are not named by the text, so I did not require tests for them. All test references are present.

text: `node` identifies the enclosing outline item. `excerpt` holds the text of the matched byte range, which may be smaller than the enclosing item.
pub fn new(node: OutlineData, excerpt: String) -> Self;
